about: The answer key of the demo case, written before any load or walk (lx-demo A). Invented content only. Each entry: a planted fact, trap or decoy; the files and strings that carry it in the built bytes (fixture_builder.py demo OUT, paths relative to OUT); the modules expected to show it; the expected match strength; what must NOT link. The walk (frontend_v2/journeys/live-demo-key.mjs) scores each entry found / missed / wrong link and is never tuned to pass. Times are Baltimore wall-clock (EDT, UTC-4) unless marked UTC.

strengths.moderate: shown as likely, with its basis
strengths.weak: shown as weak or coincidental (busy place, short overlap)

entries.statement: Travis Kell has rented bay 4 of Ruiz Auto & Tire since 1 October 2023 for a flat $650 a month, five months before the first theft.

Each $650 credit on the Ruiz Auto & Tire account (the State's 'payments from the cooperator') is the same money as the bay-rent debit on Kell's account, on the 1st of every month, January to June 2024.

entries.statement: On 8 June at 13:52 Kell called Mateo: his car had died on Ferrow Avenue. Mateo towed it to the garage (on scene 14:10, back 14:50) with Kell in the tow truck's cab. This is when the glovebox phone entered the truck.

entries.statement: The glovebox phone was with Kell's phone, at Kell's apartment in the evenings, on 14 of the 16 days from 23 May to 7 June.
After 8 June the glovebox phone is only where the tow truck worked: the Ferrow Avenue breakdown, the garage, the 10 and 12 June tow jobs, and the garage on the morning of the search.
Kell's phone has no data from 23:00 to 04:00 on each of the five theft nights: five separate gaps, not one long one.
Kell's extraction records the zone America/Chicago, but he never left Maryland. Times are read as the instants they are; nothing places him in Chicago and nothing moves by an hour.

entries.statement: Kell's badge B-11032 opened dock 3 on every theft night, including N3 to N5 after he was fired on 20 April and HR asked for the badge to be deactivated.
Okafor's badge B-20417 was in on every theft night, and his phone was at the warehouse each night.
The Telegram group 'night crew' (Kell and Okafor) sets each theft night the afternoon before; the same conversation is on both their phones.

The glovebox phone's only contacts are Okafor's second number, Marsh and Penn. On each theft night it sent 'bay 4 is clear' and 'unit's open' to Okafor and 'be on the gate at 11' to Marsh; it never holds Mateo's number.
Desmond Okafor is one person across two numbers and a Telegram account, saved as 'Dee' on Kell's phone, 'D.O.' on the glovebox phone and 'Desmond Okafor' on Brianna's.
'Mateo 🔧' on Okafor's phone is Mateo Garza, a mechanic friend on +1 443 555 0181. He is not Mateo Ruiz.

entries.statement: The State's cell-site sector 4471-2 covers the garage and Kell's apartment alike; the glovebox phone's after-midnight activity used cells at the industrial park and on Tallow Creek Road, which the opinion leaves out.
The State's discovery index lists seven extractions (E-1 to E-7) but disc 2 holds six; E-7, a second handset from Kell's vehicle, was not produced.

carriers.text: E-7 second handset recovered from T. Kell's vehicle

entries.statement: The two power tools found in the garage carry serials on no loss list; Mateo bought them at Penn's shop on 22 May for $240 (receipt, his card debit, Penn's card sale, Penn's listing).
Ten serials on Penn's marketplace listings are on the police loss lists.
Kell's April statement arrives twice (bank production and State's Exhibit 14). The second copy is a linked, set-aside duplicate; its payments are counted once.
Kell's May statement says 'Page 1 of 2' and page 2 is missing: it does not balance and waits for a person; no payment is invented for the missing page.

On Kell's March statement the 18 March cash deposit of $9,800.00 is printed as '9' and '800.00' in two pieces, so a reader may take 800.00. A correction keeps the reading visible and uses 9,800.00 in sums.
Every other statement month balances to its printed closing balance and is verified without a person (Kell Jan-Apr and Jun, the shop Oct 2023-Jun 2024, Mateo Jan-Jun).
Okafor sent Kell a voice note on 9 June at 20:03 (invented speech): 'Do not call the other phone.'

expect.speech: Hey T, it's me. They are asking around the warehouse about the badges. Do not call the other phone. I will come by tonight.

entries.statement: The five theft nights appear on the timeline on their dates (15 March, 12 April, 3 May, 17 May, 31 May 2024) from the police reports.
Entity extraction puts the people and businesses in the graph and connects Travis Kell to Stowell Self Storage, Lena Marsh, Desmond Okafor and Penn's Used Tools.
Kell's apartment and the garage are 0.9 km apart: the glovebox phone's evenings at Kell's apartment fall in the same cell sector the State reads as 'the garage'.

Workspace holds the three tasks (subpoena the storage company; interview the 12 April tow customer; request the seventh extraction), notes, pinned evidence and a motion deadline, made by the jobs login and labelled as seed.

Theories T1 (State: fence in bay 4), T2 (defence: Kell's operation; the glovebox phone entered the truck on 8 June) and T3 (Okafor as inside man) exist, each with evidence for and against from several modules.

One dossier per person (Mateo Ruiz, Travis Kell, Desmond Okafor, Brianna Cole, Lena Marsh, Gary Penn), collecting numbers, accounts and addresses; Kell's carries the proffer as an interview with AI-drafted claims left 'Drafted by <model>, not confirmed'.
Ruiz Auto & Tire (the business) and Mateo Ruiz (its owner) may link; Rosa Ruiz and Lucía Ruiz are family. None of them links to Carla Ruiz or Mateo Garza.
